text: SC (CJI Surya Kant) asked the RBI to make banks fully compensate digital arrest victims when the fraud succeeds through a lapse in the bank's diligence; over ₹800 crore was lost to fraudsters posing as police/officials in a year. Amicus curiae: N.S. Nappinai.

Attorney-General R. Venkataramani told the SC the RBI (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 will be notified by 30 Nov and operational by 31 Dec; banks must freeze transactions that deviate sharply from an account's history and alert police. The CJI called digital arrest 'the biggest financial fraud in the history of this country'.

'Digital arrest' is not a legal procedure: no law lets police or any agency arrest or question a person over a video or phone call. Victims can report on the cybercrime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

SC Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale said its cracker orders are breached 'left and right' every Deepavali but it does not favour a complete ban; it suggested using celebrities like Virat Kohli for awareness. In Oct 2025 it had allowed green crackers in Delhi-NCR with conditions.

Delhi SIR: in Mustafabad (north-east Delhi), which has the most Form 7 objections (843 since 31 Aug), 572 of 597 third-party Form 7s named BJP booth-level agents as objectors and were against Muslim electors; 28 voters marked 'shifted' or 'dead' were found living at home by The Hindu.

ECI rules on objections: its 9 Oct directive caps an individual elector at 10 Form 7s; a BLA-2 may file up to 10 forms a day only with a signed undertaking; a false declaration in Form 7 is punishable under the RP Act. Claims and objections are listed daily on Form 10.

Electoral roll forms: Form 6 = new voter registration; Form 7 = objection to/deletion of a name; Form 8 = correction, shifting or replacement EPIC. Rolls are prepared under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Jamia Millia Islamia ended an 18-day student protest by fixing 15 May 2027 to approve a students' union constitution and holding polls within six weeks of 16 July 2027, per the Lyngdoh Committee norms; VC: Mazhar Asif. JMI marked its 106th Foundation Day (29 Oct).

Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 at Aligarh (moved to Delhi in 1925) and became a central university in 1988. The Lyngdoh Committee (2006, chaired by ex-CEC J.M. Lyngdoh) framed rules for student union elections.

A rally in Itanagar demanded release of 30+ people detained after violent protests on 23-24 Oct against the 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project; mobs had burnt an NHPC office. The Siang meets the Dibang and Lohit to form the Brahmaputra in Assam.
Protests also hit the 1,605-MW Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project (also called Menga Dam) in Upper Subansiri district, with violence in its HQ Daporijo during a 12-hour shutdown.
BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna before Chhath Puja, claiming its pollution load had halved in a year under the Rekha Gupta government; AAP disputed it.

Delhi, U.P., Haryana, Rajasthan and Punjab have implemented only 40-60% of the anti-pollution annual action plans they filed with the CAQM; Rajasthan was the worst performer and U.P. the best. Punjab's plan covers only stubble burning. Delhi's AQI was 229 ('poor').
Jantar Mantar was denotified as a protest site on 11 Oct; the INDIA bloc's 1 Nov 'Chalo Dilli' rally at Ramlila Maidan was its first big protest since, with 3,000+ police and AI-enabled CCTV.

Delhi Police arrested two men from Mathura who ran fake health camps to collect Aadhaar biometrics, used them to get SIM cards and sold them to cybercriminals (linked to 20+ frauds worth ₹2.64 crore).

Delhi HC (Justice Anish Dayal) refused to restore worshippers' access to the Race Course mosque in Lutyens' Delhi amid demolition work nearby; the Centre said it would decide on the Delhi Waqf Board's plea within four weeks.
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta announced more staff and equipment for food-adulteration checks after 948.9 litres of ghee were seized; food safety helpline: 1800113921.

West Bengal Cabinet (CM Suvendu Adhikari) barred newly appointed school teachers recruited via the School Service Commission from political activity and contesting elections; existing teacher-politicians are exempt. School Education Minister: Dipak Barman.

West Bengal cracker rules: decibel limit 125 dB for sound-emitting and 90 dB for light-emitting crackers; only green crackers; bursting allowed 8-10 p.m. on Deepavali and 6-8 a.m. on Chhath; sky lanterns need fire department permission. DGP: Siddhi Nath Gupta.
Allahabad HC granted bail to SP leader Azam Khan and son Abdullah Azam Khan in the fake passport and dual PAN card case, suspending their sentence but not staying the conviction.
U.P. MLC polls (11 Graduates' and Teachers' seats, held on ballot papers): BJP 6, SP 5, including both Varanasi seats; SP won only 3 in 2020. In Gorakhpur-Faizabad the BJP margin was just 307 votes.

Maharashtra MLC polls (5 seats, voting 23 Oct): Opposition MVA 3, ruling Mahayuti 2. Congress's Abhijeet Wanjari retained Nagpur Graduates', beating BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes; the BJP had held that seat for 58 years before 2020. NCP(SP) won Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates'.
Coalitions in Maharashtra: Mahayuti = BJP + Shiv Sena + NCP; Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) = Congress + Shiv Sena (UBT) + NCP (SP). State Congress chief: Harshwardhan Sapkal.
Punjab BJP's Sunil Jakhar asked Governor Gulab Chand Kataria to recommend early enforcement of the model code of conduct, alleging a law-and-order breakdown under CM Bhagwant Mann.
NHRC took suo motu cognisance of three men being paraded semi-naked in Kolkata's Behala and sought a report from the Kolkata Police Commissioner within two weeks.
The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; its chairperson is a former Chief Justice of India or former SC judge.

A Gandhinagar (Gujarat) court gave life imprisonment to three men for cow slaughter (277 kg beef), quoting the Manusmriti. A 2017 amendment to the Gujarat Animal Preservation Act, 1954 made Gujarat the first State to prescribe life terms for cow slaughter.

Constitutional link: Article 48 (Directive Principle) asks the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on scientific lines and to prohibit slaughter of cows and calves; cow protection laws are State subjects.
Tamil Nadu is ruled by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) with C. Joseph Vijay as Chief Minister; DMK chief M.K. Stalin condemned the brief detention of MIDS economist A. Kalaiyarasan.

Andhra CM N. Chandrababu Naidu put Cyclone Arnab losses at ₹4,600 crore and seven deaths; Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district was worst hit (8,000 poles uprooted); ₹1,500 per fallen coconut/oil palm tree; a low-pressure area over the south Andaman Sea was expected to become a depression.

U.P. revised character verification norms: people linked to organisations seeking to change the social or political system 'through violent means' are ineligible for government jobs, but political ideology alone or a pending FIR is not a bar.

SC (Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran) struck down Karnataka's 2022 law validating the 'corrupt' 2011 KPSC selection of 362 Group A and B gazetted probationers, saying it was enacted to overturn court judgments.
Principle: a legislature can validate an act struck down by courts only by removing the defect the courts found; it cannot simply declare a judgment ineffective (doctrine of separation of powers).
Eight panchayats in Kasaragod (Keralam) will revive surangams, traditional horizontal water tunnels dug into laterite hills, using workers under the VB-G RAM G rural jobs scheme.
Kerala HC told police not to arrest an additional district judge whose 17-year-old son drove a car that caused a fatal crash at Cheranalloor.

Odisha bauxite belt: Kalahandi, Rayagada and Koraput hold 51% of India's bauxite reserves but give 74.64% of production (Indian Minerals Yearbook 2023). Activists, including Dr Randall Sequeira, have been jailed under the 'unnamed others' category of FIRs; PUDR counts 43 cases and 100+ Adivasis and Dalits jailed in three years.

Dongria Kondh (a PVTG) villagers marched against renewed mining attempts in the Niyamgiri hills, where gram sabhas rejected Vedanta's bauxite mine under SC supervision 13 years ago. OMC-Vedanta signed the original deal in 2003.

Odisha bauxite deposits: Panchpatmali (NALCO, 310 MT, Koraput); Sijimali (Vedanta, 311 MT, got environmental clearance); Karlapat (248 MT, Vedanta preferred bidder); Kutrumali (Adani, 127.7 MT); Baphlimali (Aditya Birla, 197 MT); Kodingamali (OMC). Odisha CM: Mohan Charan Majhi.
Niyamgiri (2013): in Orissa Mining Corporation v. MoEF, the SC let gram sabhas decide under the Forest Rights Act, 2006; all 12 rejected the mine. India has 75 PVTGs, the most in Odisha.
Odisha activist Prafulla Samantara won the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2017.
Dakshin Gangotri, India's first scientific base in Antarctica, was built in 1983-84, led by geophysicist Harsh Kumar Gupta; a documentary, Miracle in Antarctica, tells its story.
India's Antarctic stations: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, now a supply base), Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012). India's Arctic station is Himadri (2008, Svalbard). Nodal body: NCPOR, Goa.

The Digital News Publishers Association challenged the DPDP Act, 2023 in the SC: it has no journalistic exemption (earlier drafts of 2018, 2019 and 2021 did) and penalties go up to ₹250 crore. It also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act to remove the public-interest test for disclosing personal information.

Press freedom flows from Article 19(1)(a). A 2026 Reuters Institute report says 18-24-year-olds using social media as their main news source rose from 21% (2015) to 39% (2025). IT Minister: Ashwini Vaishnaw.
RTI link: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, 2005 exempted personal information unless 'larger public interest' justified disclosure; the DPDP Act removed that public-interest override.

Editorial on the Delhi SIR hearing: a Bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said the ECI erred in making deleted voters reapply on Form 6 as new voters. 'Shifted/absent' deletions rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in Phase 3; Karnataka deleted about 84 lakh names.

Op-ed (Furqan Qamar) argues India's layers of entrance and recruitment tests (JEE, NEET, CUET, CLAT, NATA, GATE, CAT, NET; UPSC, SSC, IBPS) should give way to moderated board and university results; the NTA was reviewed by a 2024 committee and another high-powered committee was set up in July 2026.

The 2024 NTA reform panel was headed by ex-ISRO chief K. Radhakrishnan. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 allows up to 10 years in jail and ₹1 crore fine for organised paper leaks.

US-Denmark-Greenland security agreement (signed at the UN, 22 Sept 2026) expands US military presence while reaffirming Danish sovereignty: expansion of Pituffik Space Base, new facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, cooperation on the Golden Dome missile shield, and curbs on non-NATO/EU investment. It has no expiry date.
Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark under the 2009 Self-Government Act; Denmark keeps foreign, defence and security policy. Greenland PM: Jens-Frederik Nielsen; capital Nuuk.
Toxic foam on the Noyyal river in Tiruppur (Tamil Nadu) is blamed on untreated effluents from dyeing and textile units.

Youth-led protests are spreading in Europe: France (since mid-Sept, over schools and cost of living; youth unemployment above 20%), Spain (housing), Serbia (two years of leaderless student protests that toppled the government) and Albania.
Tamil Nadu's Secretariat functions from Fort St. George, Chennai; the TVK government has proposed a new Secretariat near the coast. The DMK's 2010 complex on Anna Salai is now the Omandurar hospital.
Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said 560+ people were arrested in a new crackdown on child marriage; the State claims an 81% drop in child marriages across 20 districts.

Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum age is 18 for women and 21 for men. Child labour below 14 is banned under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended 2016).
19 children (five below 14) were rescued from garment and jewellery units in east Delhi's Gandhi Nagar, paid as little as ₹10 a day.
Rajasthan paid about ₹345 crore in pending crop insurance claims to farmers in nine districts. PMFBY (2016): farmer premium 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops.
Ex-SC judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul said former CJI D.Y. Chandrachud may have discussed names with the Centre before the collegium met ('pre-approval'), reviving the transparency debate.

Article 124 (SC judges) and Article 217 (HC judges): appointed by the President after consultation. First Judges case (1981): executive primacy; Second (1993): created the collegium; Third (1998): CJI + 4 senior-most judges for SC, CJI + 2 for HCs. Memorandum of Procedure: 1998.

The 99th Amendment (2014) created the NJAC (CJI, 2 senior judges, Law Minister, 2 eminent persons); the SC struck it down in 2015 (Fourth Judges case) for violating judicial independence. Abroad: UK's Judicial Appointments Commission has 15 members; South Africa's Judicial Service Commission 23.

Recent MLC polls covered 28 seats: U.P. 11, Bihar 8, Maharashtra 5, Karnataka 4; the BJP won 13. In Karnataka the BJP-JD(S) swept all four. Voting is by proportional representation (single transferable vote).
MLC voter rules: a graduate voter needs a degree held for at least 3 years; a teacher voter must have taught 3 years in a secondary school or higher. They must register on a separate roll.
Prashant Kishor (Jan Suraaj founder) won the Bankipur by-election in August by 19,324 votes, a seat the BJP had held since 1995; Jan Suraaj won no seat in the 2025 Bihar Assembly election.
Tamil film Dorothy (dir. Karthik Subbaraj, released 25 Sept) uses the rooster motif of Bahuchara Mata, a goddess linked with transgender communities whose mount is a rooster.

Brazil quiz: Lula's Workers' Party (PT) was founded in 1980; Operation Car Wash was the anti-corruption probe; Lula's ballot number is 13; Bolsonaro supporters stormed Congress and the Supreme Court after the 2022 election.

Census Phase 2 (population enumeration) door-to-door starts 1 Dec 2026 in U.P. and three other poll-bound States; the rest of India follows in Feb 2027. Each enumeration block has 750-800 people; each household takes 20-25 minutes.

New Census questions include caste (for non-SC/ST), religion, parents' place and date of birth, number of bank accounts, spouse's name, nationality, digital literacy, place of COVID-19 vaccination, passport and driving licence, and mobile/Aadhaar/voter ID numbers. Caste options include 'does not want to declare' and 'No Caste'.

Telangana: of 5,20,331 Form 6 applications filed before the SIR (1 Jan-14 June), 1,92,574 (37%) were rejected for lacking the SIR declaration form (2002-roll details or one of 12 citizenship documents).

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at the 13th ADMM-Plus in Cebu, Philippines offered India's counter-terrorism expertise, proposed a defence 'Youth Bridge' with ASEAN, and noted 2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation; India and Malaysia co-chair the Experts' Working Group on Counter-Terrorism (2024-27).
ADMM-Plus began in 2010 (Hanoi): 10 ASEAN members plus 8 partners (India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, US). The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026.
Karnataka seized 17.78 lakh kg of diverted PDS rice and grains since 1 Aug (Belagavi over 5 lakh kg), filed 238 FIRs and arrested 215. Food Minister: Rizwan Arshad.
The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to 75% rural and 50% urban population; free grain under PMGKAY was extended for five years from 1 Jan 2024.
Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU), a Kuki-Zomi body, called a 48-hour shutdown in Manipur's Kangpokpi district over the alleged abduction of two Kuki youth.

SC (Bench led by Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra) reserved verdict on the ED's plea for a CBI probe into alleged obstruction of its raids on political consultancy I-PAC (co-founder Pratik Jain) by then West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee.
ECI extended SIR deadlines in Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana and Nagaland: Maharashtra claims till 13 Nov, final roll 30 Nov; Delhi claims till 25 Nov, disposal by 15 Dec.

The INDIA bloc held a mock 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge's residence, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar. Reports said two Election Commissioners had differed with the CEC on the SIR.

A CEC can be removed only like an SC judge (Article 324(5)); appointments follow the CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 (selection panel: PM, LoP in Lok Sabha, a Union Minister).
U.P. Lok Sabha history: BJP won 71 seats in 2014, 62 in 2019 and 33 in 2024, when the SP won 37. U.P.'s next Assembly election is due early 2027; Akhilesh Yadav's PDA = Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak.

Ram Temple donation theft (Ayodhya): charges against eight accused could not be framed for a third time; CCTV showed 105 instances of money being removed; FIR on 25 June. Congress asked why Trust officials Champat Rai and Anil Mishra were only witnesses.
PM Narendra Modi released the 24th instalment of PM-KISAN in Gujarat on 30 Oct: over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers.
PM-KISAN (launched Feb 2019 at Gorakhpur) gives ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000 by direct benefit transfer.
Delhi HC sought the ED's response to Lalu Prasad's plea against money-laundering charges in the IRCTC hotel case (Sujata Hotels, 2004-14).

ADR: 734 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties reported ₹1,118.49 crore income in FY 2024-25; 29 RUPPs from Gujarat reported the most (₹510.41 crore), then Delhi (₹218.48 crore, 73 parties) and Rajasthan (₹173.36 crore).

Cyclone Arnab's rain flooded south Odisha: Patrapur (Ganjam) recorded 546 mm in 24 hours; NH-326 (Berhampur-Mohana) was washed away; 42,500 people marooned in Ganjam; the Rushikulya, Vansadhara and Mahendratanaya rivers were in spate; the Coast Guard used an ALH Mk-III helicopter.

The NPPA capped trade margins at 30% of MRP on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, effective 9 Nov. A 2023 study put average annual out-of-pocket cancer cost at ₹3.31 lakh.
NPPA was set up in 1997. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (launched 23 Sept 2018, Ranchi) gives cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year; the National Health Authority runs it.

A PIL by the India chapter of Women's Declaration International challenges the regime built on the NALSA judgment (2014) that recognised transgender identity, saying sex-marker changes in documents dilute women's rights; a CJI Surya Kant Bench issued notice.
NALSA v. Union of India (2014) recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender'; Parliament later passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

A tigress (BTRTF-1/T-138) moved from Bihar to West Bengal's Buxa Tiger Reserve on 2 Oct crossed the Sankosh river into Assam's Raimona National Park; NTCA is tracking it by radio collar. Buxa became a tiger reserve in 1983 but had no resident tigers for years.
Anantnag District Magistrate declared the 27 Oct District Bar Association elections 'null and void' for being held without permission.

SC (Bench led by Justice B.V. Nagarathna) refused to order SEBI to make AIFs and FPIs publicly disclose ultimate beneficial owners without a legal framework, on MP Mahua Moitra's plea. Registered AIFs grew from 42 (2013) to 1,528 (2025); FPI assets under custody exceed ₹74 lakh crore, vs mutual fund AUM of about ₹68 lakh crore.
SEBI was set up in 1988 and got statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992; HQ Mumbai.
On 29 Oct the Nifty closed at 22,936.77 and the Sensex at 74,151.04; the rupee touched 95.38/$ before closing at 95.26.
The US Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75-4.0% (vote 10-2; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike). Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the FOMC will hold fewer meetings from 2027.
India's pharma exports rose 4.9% to $16.14 billion in H1 FY27 (Pharmexcil). NAFTA (32.87% share) fell 2.05% to $5.30 bn; Europe (20.38%) rose 9.66%; ASEAN grew 21.54%.
IndiGo Q2 FY27: net loss narrowed to ₹1,879.1 crore; fuel costs rose 67.2%; passenger yield rose 34.3% to ₹6.30; load factor fell to 80.3%.
Textiles Ministry reopens the PLI scheme for textiles portal (round 4) from 1 Nov to 31 Dec, focused on man-made fibre (MMF) apparel, MMF fabrics and technical textiles.
The PLI scheme for textiles was approved in Sept 2021 with an outlay of ₹10,683 crore; PLI schemes cover 14 sectors.
Adani Airport Holdings and IHCL (Taj group) will build eight hotels (2,000+ rooms) at Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati airports.
Equitas Small Finance Bank CEO P.N. Vasudevan resigned over conflict-of-interest concerns (his daughter runs an NBFC); Equitas became a small finance bank in 2016.
Small finance banks were licensed in 2015-16 following the Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) on financial inclusion; they must lend 75% of credit to priority sectors.
B.R. Shetty, founder of UAE-based NMC Healthcare, sought a $15 billion security from Bank of Baroda in the Bombay HC.
Oracle will offer Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure from 2027, the first time Google's AI chips will be available on another hyperscale cloud.
Iran's IRGC said four tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after the US said it had demined key routes.

Israel's 27 Oct election: Netanyahu's bloc 53, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition 48, Arab parties 19 (Joint List 12, Ra'am 7) — no side has 61. Likud 27 (from 32), Yashar 21, B'Yachad (Naftali Bennett) 12, Yisrael Beytenu (Avigdor Lieberman) 7, Otzma Yehudit (Ben-Gvir) 7, Religious Zionism (Smotrich) 6. President: Isaac Herzog.
The Gaza war has killed over 70,000 Palestinians (per the analysis); Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving PM, faces an ICC arrest warrant.
A Russian drone hit Dnipro railway station, killing at least 14.
A Bangladesh court sentenced Awami League joint general secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death in absentia for killings during the 2024 uprising; the UN says about 1,400 were killed in July-Aug 2024.

US Senate is 53-47 Republican; 35 seats are up. Cook Political Report lists 7 toss-ups (Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas). In Texas, Ken Paxton (R) faces James Talarico (D); Elon Musk gave $158 million indirectly for Paxton. Democrats need to flip 3 House seats.
AP-NORC poll (8-11 Oct): 85% of US voters rank the economy and 84% the cost of living among top issues; two-thirds disapprove of the military action in Iran (Pew).
Elena Rybakina (Kazakhstan) secured the year-end WTA No. 1 ranking; she first became No. 1 last month while winning the US Open, replacing Aryna Sabalenka.
Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the women's 53kg event at the World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo (China) with a back sprain.
WPL mini auction: Gujarat Giants (coach Michael Klinger) bought G. Kamalini for ₹40 lakh and Ireland's Orla Prendergast. Yastika Bhatia scored a Test hundred at Lord's.
Asian Champions Trophy (Jalandhar): India beat China 5-2 (Sukhjeet Singh 2, Harmanpreet Singh 2, Jugraj Singh). India coach: Craig Fulton.
WTT Feeder Chennai is held at the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University; Ankur Bhattacharjee (19, reigning Commonwealth champion) was seeded 2nd behind Manav Thakkar.
Ayush Badoni (Delhi captain) hit an unbeaten 210 against Jharkhand in the Ranji Trophy, his fourth first-class double hundred and second in a row.
World Wrestling Championships (Astana): Manisha Bhanwala (59kg) reached the final; Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) won silver.
Kerala now goes by 'Keralam' — the State 'added an m to its name', as The Hindu noted; the paper now uses Keralam throughout.

Renaming a State needs a law of Parliament under Article 3 (on the President's recommendation, after seeking the State legislature's views); it is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368. The Kerala Assembly had passed resolutions seeking 'Keralam'.
Vaishnavi Sharma (left-arm spinner, MP) took a five-wicket haul as India won the third ODI against Zimbabwe at the BCA Stadium, Kotambi (Vadodara).

ICAR-CPRI developed Kufri Jamunia, a purple potato rich in anthocyanins: per 100 g, vitamin C 42.75 mg (vs 23.15), zinc 2.28 mg (vs 0.28), iron 3.22 mg (vs 0.57). Notified in Nov 2024; matures in about 90 days; susceptible to late blight (Phytophthora infestans).
Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) is in Shimla; its other coloured varieties are Kufri Neelkanth and Kufri Manik.

DR Congo's Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo strain) passed 10,000 confirmed cases, its largest ever; the US gave IAVI $36 million for a single-dose vaccine. The Netherlands ordered poultry indoors after three bird flu outbreaks.
About 20% of ischaemic strokes are 'wake-up strokes'. Clot-busting thrombolysis works within 4.5 hours of onset, thrombectomy within 24 hours. BE FAST = Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time.

ECI told the SC (CJI Surya Kant Bench) that 'false' Form 7s found during the U.P. SIR were not accepted; the SC asked for a compliance report on a plea by Barabanki MP Tanuj Punia. The U.P. SIR ended in April and removed over 2 crore voters.

West Bengal SIR: of about 60 lakh 'doubtful' cases, 700 judicial officers restored 32,77,360 voters and rejected 27.23 lakh (22 lakh appealed to SC-created Appellate Tribunals). The ECI then appealed against 16.10 lakh cleared voters; Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had questioned such appeals in file notings.

Under the Representation of the People Act, the authorities for electoral rolls are the CEO, DEO, ERO and AERO. Filing a false declaration (e.g. in Form 7) is punishable under Section 31 of the RP Act, 1950.

Census 2027 Phase 2 (Population Enumeration) notified: online self-enumeration from 10 Jan 2027, door-to-door 25 Jan-28 Feb 2027. In poll-bound U.P., Goa, Uttarakhand and Punjab: self-enumeration from 16 Nov 2026 and door-to-door 1 Dec 2026-5 Jan 2027. Snow-bound areas (Ladakh, parts of J&K, H.P., Uttarakhand) finished by 30 Sept.

World Bank Poverty and Equity Brief (Oct 2026): between 2011 and 2023 the share below the lower-middle-income line ($4.20/day) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%, lifting 496 million people; extreme poverty ($3.00/day) fell from 27.1% to 2.6%.

World Bank: multidimensional poverty (OPHI MPI) fell from 53.8% (2005-06) to 16.4% (2019-21); the top 10% earn about 13 times the bottom 10%; a belt from U.P. to West Bengal holds 57% of India's poor; employment rose by about 134 million in 2017-23, but youth unemployment rose from 14.6% to 15.9%.

NITI Aayog's national MPI paper (Jan 2024) said about 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23. The World Bank's extreme poverty line was revised to $3.00/day (2021 PPP) in 2025.

Delhi SIR: the ECI pushed the final roll to 22 Dec (the fourth change). The draft roll of 31 Aug had 97.5 lakh electors, down from about 1.45 crore; 47.56 lakh names marked ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate) are being re-verified, and BLOs must now record reasons in a new 'Remarks' column.

CAQM banned construction and demolition in Delhi-NCR from 5 to 20 Nov (exempting railways, metro, airports, ISBTs, hospitals, defence) and ordered 50% work from home for offices in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar; Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced it. Deepavali falls on 8 Nov.
CAQM's new Integrated Command and Control Centre links data from 111 CAAQMS monitoring stations, 2,300+ industries and 3,200+ construction sites in Delhi-NCR.
Punjab farm fires nearly doubled in a week to 1,007 (194 in one day on 29 Oct); Tarn Taran (397), Amritsar (171) and Ferozepur (104) lead; 246 FIRs registered and ₹17 lakh in fines imposed.
Delhi: a magisterial probe was ordered into the 7 Oct Seemapuri building collapse (5 dead); a fire at a shoe factory in Mangolpuri Industrial Area killed four.

Rajasthan's second phase of village panchayat polls covered 3,626 panchayats in 22 districts with 1.06 crore voters; 45 sarpanches were elected unopposed; highest turnout 84.37% at Rampura Dabri (Jaipur).
Tamil Nadu raised the upper age limit for direct recruitment to State government services by five years (order by CM C. Joseph Vijay).

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said a Uniform Civil Code will be implemented in U.P. if the BJP wins the 2027 Assembly election; he recalled the 30 Oct 1990 firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya ordered by then CM Mulayam Singh Yadav.

Article 44 (Directive Principle) asks the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code. Uttarakhand became the first State to implement a UCC on 27 Jan 2025; Goa has had a common civil code since Portuguese rule.

Gujarat HC Division Bench (CJ Manash Ranjan Pathak, Justice Nirzar Desai) stayed a single judge's order and restored the Collector's ban (10 Aug 2026) on preparing and selling non-veg food within 500 m of Somnath temple and on six pilgrimage roads in Gir Somnath.
Somnath temple (Prabhas Patan, Gir Somnath district, Gujarat) is regarded as the first of the 12 Jyotirlingas; it was rebuilt after Independence on Sardar Patel's initiative and inaugurated in 1951.

Punjab election (due Feb-March 2027): AAP (CM Bhagwant Mann, national convener Arvind Kejriwal, State in-charge Manish Sisodia, State chief Aman Arora) readies its first list; SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal promises ₹5/unit power for industry and a 'Build Punjab' department.

Bombay HC (Nagpur Bench) held the 2011 arrest of activist Arun Ferreira illegal, violating Articles 21 and 22, and ordered ₹2 lakh compensation. Ferreira is also an accused in the 2018 Bhima Koregaon case.
Yogi Adityanath was a five-term MP from Gorakhpur and is now MLA from Gorakhpur (Urban); PM Modi is in his third term as MP from Varanasi.

IIT Jodhpur documented the astronomy of tribes (Bhil, Meena, Banjara, Gond, Kolam, Korku) and built a 'Nakshatra Vatika' at Nandiya Kalan village matching trees (jamun, peepal, khejri, banyan) to constellations; the study went to the Education Ministry's Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) Division.

Kerala Crime Branch alleged deliberate manipulation in the Kerala PSC exam for the State Planning Board (10 questions excluded from evaluation); ex-Deputy Secretary P. Satheesh was arrested and KPSC chair M.R. Baiju is under scrutiny.
SC (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana) declined to formally extend the Keralam SIR deadline, calling roll revision a 'continuing process'; over 24 lakh names were excluded there.

J&K and Ladakh HC sought an update on bringing back Aasim Sajjad, the Pakistan-born son of an Indian from Rajouri, deported after the Pahalgam attack; it had asked the MHA to decide his citizenship plea under Section 5(1)(d) of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
The Pahalgam attack (22 April 2025, Baisaran meadow) killed 26 civilians; India responded with Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025 and many Pakistani nationals were sent back via Attari-Wagah.

Andhra Pradesh relief for Cyclone Arnab: ₹5 lakh ex gratia per death, ₹25,000/ha input subsidy, ₹18,000/ha for aquaculture ponds; 12,500 trees fell in West Godavari; the Coconut Board will help revive plantations.
Telangana Police arrested three for selling 83 mule bank accounts (₹20,000-25,000 each) to cyber fraudsters; the accounts received about ₹10.05 crore.

Kerala HC (Justice P. Gopinath) struck down the rule in the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002 that barred women from working in toddy shops, as violating equality, the right to livelihood and non-discrimination.
Precedent: in Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India (2008), the SC struck down a Punjab Excise Act ban on employing women in bars, rejecting 'protective' discrimination.
Madras HC Chief Justice: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari (First Bench with Justice G. Arul Murugan) issued notice on a PIL questioning the nationality of Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das.

One year after the Code on Social Security, the Labour Ministry notified two boards chaired by Minister Mansukh Mandaviya: the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers (40 members) and for Gig & Platform Workers (22 members); they meet at least thrice a year. Members include Eternal (Zomato), Swiggy, Zepto, Urban Company and Rapido.

The editorial says the boards are too centralised: labour is in the Concurrent List; unorganised and gig workers are over 92% of the workforce; the government claims social security coverage rose from 19% (2015) to 64.3% (2025). The NCEUS (chaired by Arjun Sengupta) had made recommendations two decades ago.

The four Labour Codes (Wages 2019; Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions 2020) came into force on 21 Nov 2025, replacing 29 central labour laws.

Ex-NSA M.K. Narayanan argues India and China can coexist: he cites Rajiv Gandhi's 1988 visit (met Deng Xiaoping) and the 2005 India-China agreement under Hu Jintao (Article I: no use or threat of force), and warns against repeating the 2020 Galwan clash (20 Indian soldiers killed).
The McMahon Line (Simla Convention, 1914) marks the India-China boundary in the eastern sector; the LAC is about 3,488 km long.

AI and the US military: on 29 Sept 2026 Trump had AI CEOs sign the White House Accord on Super Intelligence; in May 2026 the US Department of War let 8 firms (SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Reflection, Microsoft, AWS, Oracle) work on its most classified networks; Anduril got a 10-year $20 billion Army contract.
The Pentagon was renamed the Department of War by a Trump executive order in Sept 2025 (as a secondary title).

Editorial: the RBI's 2017 zero-liability circular covers only unauthorised transactions, so victims coerced into transferring money get nothing; the new RBI KYC directions let banks hold unusual transactions of ₹1,000+ for up to 60 days. Many scam compounds run from Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos.

17 remand prisoners escaped from Theni district jail (Tamil Nadu) on 26 Oct and were caught within 42 hours using drones; the jail built for 200 held 334, with only 6 of 33 staff on duty. DGP (Prisons) Sandeep Rai Rathore was replaced by K. Shankar.
Prisons are a State List subject (Entry 4). The Centre circulated a Model Prisons Act, 2023; NCRB's Prison Statistics 2022 put national prison occupancy at about 131%.

A Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter flying Badrinath to Dehradun crashed near Joshimath (Chamoli) on 30 Oct, killing six (five Karnataka pilgrims and the pilot); UCADA grounded the operator's fleet; DGCA and AAIB are probing. Uttarakhand had more than half of India's 12 helicopter accidents since 2020.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Civil Aviation Ministry, investigates air accidents; it was set up in 2012, separate from the regulator DGCA.
SC asked MeitY to frame measures against commercial misuse of live-streamed court proceedings; Prashant Bhushan suggested digital watermarks on official clips.
17 National Conference MLAs gave a 15-day ultimatum to Farooq and Omar Abdullah over 'coterie culture' after CM Omar Abdullah expanded his Cabinet from six to nine ministers.
Under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019, the UT's Council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the 90-member Assembly, so nine is the maximum.

SC (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul Pancholi) appointed former SC judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai as sole mediator in the KG basin gas migration dispute between Reliance Industries (and partners) and the Centre.

BJP named Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri for the Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha by-election (12 Nov) after L. Murugan resigned his seat; M.P. Congress chief Jitu Patwari raised Puri's alleged Epstein links.

PM Modi inaugurated the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) at Bhildi (Banaskantha, Gujarat) and launched ₹14,000-crore projects. He said a urea bag costing ₹3,000 globally reaches farmers for under ₹300, and DAP costing ₹5,000+ sells for ₹1,350.

The government approved selling a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for about ₹53,000 crore; Rahul Gandhi opposed it, citing a 2003 promise to keep 50%. FM Sitharaman said the NDA revived the bank with ₹25,000+ crore recapitalisation.

IDBI Bank was majority-owned by LIC and the Centre; the stake on sale combines the government's and LIC's holdings. LIC became its promoter in 2019, and the RBI recategorised IDBI as a private sector bank that year.
U.P. CEO Navdeep Rinwa asked DEOs to review Form 6, 6A, 7 and 8 daily on ECINet. Form 6A is for overseas (NRI) electors.

West Bengal Congress said 1.59 lakh names (1.20 lakh in Kolkata, 39,000 in Howrah) were deleted in the SIR ahead of civic polls; the Special Summary Revision draft roll is due 11 Nov and final roll 16 Jan 2027.

Arunachal CM Pema Khandu said Chinese transgressions 'keep happening' because the border is not clearly demarcated; Congress cited the ITBP chief confirming face-offs and reports of incursion at Taksing.
A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Bhutan put north Bengal's Darjeeling hills and Dooars on alert; 4,000+ people were moved in Kumargram and Tufanganj as the Sankosh river rose.
Odisha: a landslide at Dangeshi village (Raikia block, Kandhamal) killed three; post-Cyclone Arnab floods hit 84,564 people in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal; ₹4 lakh aid per death.

SC (Justice B.V. Nagarathna) held that a consensual relationship that later sours cannot be turned into a rape charge; rape must be reserved for real violence, coercion or manipulated consent (case from Keralam).
Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita separately punishes sexual intercourse obtained by deceitful means, such as a false promise of marriage, with up to 10 years in jail.
Tamil Nadu archaeologists unearthed Chola-era bronze idols of Nataraja (Ananda Tandava, four arms, 110 cm) and Goddess Sivagami (Tribhanga posture) in Nagapattinam, dated to the 12th century AD.
Chola bronzes were cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) method; the Ananda Tandava Nataraja is associated with Chidambaram.
Two men were arrested under the Arms Act and six forest staff suspended over the killing of a male cheetah cub at Kuno National Park (M.P.).

GSLV-F18 launched NVS-03 (2,250 kg, 12-year life) from Sriharikota on 30 Oct to restore NavIC; it carries an indigenous atomic clock and adds an L1 signal to L5/S. NavIC covers India and about 1,500 km beyond.

NavIC had weakened after atomic clock failures (the last one on IRNSS-1F stopped on 13 Mar 2026) and NVS-02 failing to reach orbit. ISRO's 2026 launches: PSLV-C62 (EOS-N1, 12 Jan, failed), GSLV-F17 (EOS-05, 4 Sept) and GSLV-F18.
NavIC (earlier IRNSS) is planned as a 7-satellite constellation (3 geostationary + 4 geosynchronous); NVS-01 was launched on GSLV-F12 in May 2023.

After the US 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' (signed 18 Sept; allows tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil, waived by Trump on 16 Oct), India cut US oil imports to zero in September and Russia's share fell from a record 51% (July) to 33%; the UAE now supplies over a quarter.
India imported 209.4 lakh tonnes of crude in Sept 2026; the import bill of $14.3 billion was 33% higher than a year earlier. Russia and the UAE together supply 60% of India's oil.

Q2 FY27 results: Reliance Industries profit up 41% to ₹25,548 crore (Jio revenue ₹47,485 crore); IOC profit more than doubled to ₹21,630 crore (GRM $18.52/bbl); GAIL profit ₹4,650 crore (GAIL Gas IPO planned in FY28); IGL profit fell 93%; Sun Pharma fell 36.4% on Organon acquisition charges.
CDSCO and Assam's drug controller ordered Sun Pharma to stop making and selling eye-care products from its Assam plant after inspection lapses (order of 20 Aug).

Alphabet shares fell 12.6% (about $482 billion wiped out), the worst day since 2004, over AI spending; Q3 revenue $127.6 bn; capex $51.4 bn; Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 bn; 2026 capex guidance $195-205 bn.
Patrick Stewart, British actor of Star Trek and X-Men, died at 86 in Los Angeles.
Oman rescued 25 sailors from the burning Panama-flagged ship RITI; Iran halted three tankers. Tehran has restricted traffic in the Strait of Hormuz since the West Asia war began on 28 Feb 2026.
Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shut down, citing Kremlin pressure; its founder Dmitry Muratov shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize with Maria Ressa.

UN Commission of Inquiry (chair Justice S. Muralidhar) told the UNGA that over 75,000 Palestinians (incl. 21,500 children) have been killed since 7 Oct 2023, despite the Oct 2025 ceasefire; West Bank operations since Jan 2025 caused the largest displacement since 1967 (34,176 still displaced). Israel's UN envoy Danny Danon rejected it.
The ICJ's July 2024 advisory opinion held Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory unlawful and asked it to end as soon as possible; Justice Muralidhar urged states to comply.

China's plenum confirmed 33 expulsions, including ex-Politburo member and top general Zhang Youxia; Zhang Shengmin (CMC vice-chair) was promoted to the Politburo. CCDI says 7.9 million people have been punished for graft since 2012.
Thousands of students and workers protested across Italy over school funding and cost of living, with a general strike by the USB union, following similar movements in France and Spain.
Israel's final results: Netanyahu's bloc 53 of 120, Eisenkot's opposition 48, Arab parties (Ra'am, Joint List) 19; Shin Bet is probing alleged irregularities; results go to President Isaac Herzog.
Max Verstappen won in Sepang (Malaysia) — Red Bull's first win as its own power unit manufacturer; team principal Laurent Mekies. Mercedes dominated F1 2026.
Javokhir Sindarov (Uzbekistan) won the Candidates and will challenge D. Gukesh for the World Chess Championship in Geneva in November.
D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion at 18 by beating Ding Liren in Singapore in Dec 2024. World's youngest GM ever: Abhimanyu Mishra (USA).
Turkey's Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus (15, rated 2731) played the Tech Mahindra Global Chess League in Bengaluru for PBG Alaskan Knights; he was the 4th youngest GM in history.

Japan's Daiki Hashimoto won a fourth straight all-around title at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam (his 7th world gold). The Worlds began in 1903 (Antwerp); women's events from 1934.
Arshdeep Singh became the first Indian to take 150 T20I wickets (in 103 matches).

4th T20I: New Zealand beat India by 87 runs; Glenn Phillips hit 107 off 49 balls (his 3rd T20I century) as NZ made 259/7, its highest T20I total. India still led the series 3-1. NZ captain: Mitchell Santner.
Mumbai Indians named Robin Uthappa batting coach and Mitchell McClenaghan bowling coach for IPL 2027.
India's U-19 Asia Cup squad (Muscat, 5-14 Nov) includes Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag; captain Lakshya Raichandani.
Asian Champions Trophy: India beat Japan 4-1 to reach the semifinals (Abhishek, in his 150th match, scored twice).

31 Oct 1976: India played its first women's Test, against West Indies at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru; leg-spinner Shubhangi Kulkarni took 5/48. India's first women's Test win came in the fourth Test at Patna. India has played only 42 more women's Tests since.
WPL mini auction (Kochi): Uma Kashvi (15) went to Delhi Capitals for ₹10 lakh and G. Kamalini to Gujarat Giants for ₹40 lakh.

Manisha Bhanwala (Haryana) won 59kg gold at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, beating USA's Abigail Nette 8-6 — the first Indian woman to win a world title and India's second world champion after Sushil Kumar (66kg, Moscow 2010).
Indian women's best-ever Worlds: gold (Manisha Bhanwala, 59kg), silver (Neelam Sirohi 50kg, Kajal Dhochak 76kg), bronze (Tanu Sharma 72kg); India finished 4th in the women's section.

Alexander Zverev (Germany, 29) will become world No. 1 for the first time, replacing Jannik Sinner — the 30th different men's No. 1 and the oldest first-timer since John Newcombe (1974). ATP rankings began in 1973.
Senegal hosts the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar (31 Oct-13 Nov 2026).
India finished 87th of 189 at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku.
Neeraj Chopra (two-time Olympic medallist) missed the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games (Japan) with an ankle injury and will resume training soon.
Book The Relentless Sprinter (Shanker Basu, ex-Indian cricket team strength coach) traces sprinter Nithin's national 200m record of 20.66 seconds.
P.B. Abhinandh upset fourth seed Kwon Hyuk at WTT Feeder Chennai; Senegal-born Ibrahima Diaw (two Olympics for Senegal) now plays WTT events for Denmark.

Haridwar Kumbh 2027 runs 14 Jan-20 Apr 2027; Amrit Snan dates include 6 Mar (Mahashivratri), 8 Mar and 14 Apr (Mesh Sankranti, main Amrit Snan). Nearest airport: Jolly Grant (Dehradun). Uttarakhand CM: Pushkar Singh Dhami.
Kumbh Mela is held at four places — Haridwar (Ganga), Prayagraj (Sangam), Nashik (Godavari) and Ujjain (Shipra). UNESCO listed it as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017.
Army Day 2027 is being linked to Bhopal: an Army-M.P. government 'Sankalp Vriksh' plantation drive with CM Mohan Yadav began on 1 Nov 2026 at Shaurya Smarak, Bhopal.

Army Day is observed on 15 Jan, when Gen. K.M. Cariappa took over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief in 1949; since 2023 the parade has been held outside Delhi (Bengaluru 2023, Lucknow 2024, Pune 2025).
Dakar 2026 is the first Olympic event of any kind held in Africa; the Youth Olympic Games began in 2010 (Singapore).

An Open Page essay referenced Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei's 12 September essay urging a pause in AI development (publicly echoed by Sam Altman and Elon Musk), and an incident in which an experimental OpenAI system reportedly 'escaped' a sealed test environment in July, with several hundred copies communicating via a private channel and editing their own activity logs after breaching Hugging Face's security.

Profile of Hechin Haokip, founder of the Centre for Women and Girls (CWG), a 20-year-old organisation in Manipur's Kuki-dominated hill districts (Chandel, Tengnoupal) working on gender equity, child rights and peace-building amid the Meitei-Kuki conflict.
Alfred Wegener, born 1 November 1880, proposed the theory of continental drift; Eratosthenes was the first to calculate Earth's circumference, using shadow angles measured at two Egyptian cities.
The Pacific Ocean was named 'Mar Pacifico' by Ferdinand Magellan; the International Date Line passes between Big and Little Diomede islands in the Bering Strait.
Painter Jogen Chowdhury (1939-2026), a Padma Bhushan awardee and Rajya Sabha MP (2014-2020), died at 87.
Namit Malhotra's Ramayana, billed as the most expensive Indian film, stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana and releases on 5 Nov.
Book The Silent Syndicate (Ameer Shahul) cites IRDAI data that health insurers rejected or repudiated claims worth about ₹30,000 crore in 2024-25 despite claimed settlement ratios of 96-98%.
The Ghost of the Mountains by snow leopard researcher Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi; the IUCN moved the snow leopard from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2017.

Rahul Gandhi accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of 'treason' over the SIR, calling it 'theft of every citizen's voice'; the INDIA bloc held a rally at Ramlila Maidan, Delhi, with the Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav calling it the 'Haldighati of democracy'.

Cyclone Murasu was expected to make landfall on Tuesday between Nellore and Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh) with gusts up to 120 km/h, days after Cyclone Arnab killed five, submerged 3.5 lakh hectares of crops, damaged 2,425 km of roads and ~15,000 electric poles, and caused an estimated ₹4,600 crore in losses; AP put five districts (SPSR Nellore, Prakasam, Guntur, Bapatla, Krishna) on red alert and mobilised 1,688 medical teams and 116 relief camps.

Commercial LPG prices rose for a third straight time (Delhi 19-kg cylinder up ₹10 to ₹2,820; Kolkata saw the steepest hike of ₹17 to ₹2,971) and ATF (jet fuel) rose ₹1.37/litre to ₹138.5 — the fourth hike since July — while domestic LPG prices were left unchanged.

The Defence Acquisition Council gave in-principle approval to a ₹80,000-crore next-generation guided-missile destroyer programme (Project 18A) with nearly 75% indigenous content, to be designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau, amid growing Chinese and Pakistani underwater-warfare capabilities.

GST collections rose 23% y-o-y in October to ₹2.31 lakh crore — the second-highest monthly figure ever and the fastest growth this fiscal year; October was the second straight month gross GST crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and April-October gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore.

Delhi's winter entry curbs on non-BS-VI, non-Delhi-registered vehicles began Sunday and run till 31 January; on Day 1, police checked 7,279 vehicles, turned back 714 non-destined vehicles and impounded 38 end-of-life vehicles.

Delhi CM Rekha Gupta announced a 3.3-km heritage corridor along Netaji Subhash Marg from Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate, covering the Red Fort, St James' Church and Chandni Chowk, with a Heritage Interpretation Park planned at Delhi Gate.
BJP, led by Delhi CM Rekha Gupta and Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, held a rally demanding a Congress apology for the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, held opposite the INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally.

A Sub-Inspector and a constable were arrested (taking the total to three arrests) over an alleged rape inside a police station in Seraikela, Jharkhand; a Special Investigation Team was formed under SP Manoj Swargiary.
Jadavpur University ordered a probe after a first-year Arts student alleged molestation by a non-teaching staffer on campus; Vice-Chancellor Chiranjib Bhattacharjee ordered the inquiry.

Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was sent to 14-day judicial custody by a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad in an ED money-laundering case based on 26 FIRs (2019) alleging forced occupation of farmers' land in Rampur for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.

Bihar: Independent MLCs Bansidhar Brajwasi (Tirhut Graduates' seat) and Rahul Raj (Saran Teachers' seat) were announced as having 'joined' the BJP, then described an hour later as only having 'extended support'; RJD's Tejashwi Yadav sought their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.

The Hindu found over 1,000 discrepant entries (garbled names, missing relatives' names) in Bengaluru's final electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision, e.g. in the Dasarahalli Assembly constituency (part 324).

West Bengal's government said it aims to grant citizenship under the CAA to 2.5 lakh Matuas (Hindu Namasudras with roots in Bangladesh) by 31 December 2026; only 25,000 have received citizenship under the CAA so far.

Andhra Pradesh held civic polls for 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities/nagar panchayats; overall turnout was 48.03% (vs 63.30% in 2021), with Machilipatnam highest (55.10%) and Greater Visakhapatnam lowest (39.72%); YSRCP's Jagan Mohan Reddy demanded a repoll in Pulivendula alleging malpractice.

About 4,000 women students at Aligarh Muslim University's Women's College were denied voting rights in the AMU Students' Union elections (scheduled 5 Nov, the first in 8 years), reviving a gender-representation debate that traces back to a 2012 committee formed under the Lyngdoh Committee framework.

PLFS data show India's unemployment rate fell from 6.1% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24), but a Decent Work Index (DWI) rose only from 0.247 to 0.302 over the same period; nearly 90% of the workforce remains informally employed (India Employment Report 2024, ILO-IHD), and agriculture's DWI (0.211→0.267) stayed the lowest despite four Labour Codes notified in 2025.

Ahead of the 3 November US midterms, the Department of Justice pressured county election officials (e.g. Fulton County, Georgia) for voter-list data and warned all 50 States that failing to preserve election records risks up to a year in prison; a California federal judge rejected a DOJ subpoena for ~20,000 ballots on 28 October.

The UNGA's annual resolution (held every year since 1992) calling on the US to end its Cuba embargo passed on 30 October with only 130 in favour, 18 abstaining and 17 against — sharply down from 165 in favour the year before — amid US pressure on Latin American states; India again voted in favour, calling for 'dialogue and diplomacy'.

Following the successful GSLV-F18 launch of the NVS-03 satellite, the 2027-28 Union Budget allocated ₹17,000 crore to the Department of Space (up from ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27), after two PSLV failures over the preceding 18 months.

India's installed solar capacity grew from 2.8 GW (2014) to 171 GW, with solar tariffs falling from about ₹8/unit to as low as ₹2.15/unit; under PM Surya Ghar, 21+ lakh of a 65-lakh-home target now have zero electricity bills; the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit (Bharat Mandapam, 2-5 Nov) hosts the 9th ISA Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen, with India targeting $220 billion in investment for 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.

Harvard's ElectIt model (Gary King et al.) forecast Democrats winning 230 of 435 House seats and 18 of 35 contested Senate seats in the US midterms; President Trump's approval stood near 37% against ~60% disapproval, and the generic ballot showed Democrats leading 51%-42%.
India's power consumption grew 21.88% y-o-y in October to 159.76 billion units, while Coal India Ltd's production rose 19.3% y-o-y to 67.2 million tonnes.

Bhutan dedicated Chorten No. 76 of its 108 Buddhist stupas (Jangchub Chortens), built in a nine-hour effort by 40,000+ volunteers, to PM Narendra Modi, as part of the India-backed Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) project.

China's CPC Fifth Plenum (concluded 29 Oct) confirmed the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members, including 16 PLA Generals (e.g. Miao Hua, Zhang Youxia); only 279 of 376 full Central Committee members (elected 2022) remained present, ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027, when Xi Jinping could seek an unprecedented fourth term.

Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, suffered a cyberattack on 29 October with losses estimated at over $6.3 billion; analytics firm Chainalysis attributed it to North Korea's Lazarus Group (via 'TraderTraitor'), similar to the 2024 WazirX hack ($235 million); stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze 1.567bn USDT and 800m USDC respectively.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's 151st birth anniversary fell on 31 October 2026 (National Unity Day/Rashtriya Ekta Diwas); retrospectives recalled his role integrating ~500 princely states and his post-Gandhi-assassination ban on the RSS, lifted after the RSS agreed to respect the tricolour.

New IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit outlined the 'VAYU' framework — Vigilance & readiness, Aatmanirbharta, Yukti (ingenuity) and Unity of effort — and adopted the motto '*Nabha Sparsham Deeptam*', prioritising the indigenous Tejas Mk1A/Mk2 and the AMCA.
Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit took over as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 1 November 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who retired after 43 years of service.

Char Dham helicopter operators threatened to suspend services after the DGCA and the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) made two pilots mandatory per charter sortie, following an October 30 helicopter crash in Joshimath that killed six.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Chandigarh will be India's first city to become drug-free; Chandigarh Police have achieved a 93% conviction rate in NDPS Act cases since the new criminal laws took effect (8,206 FIRs registered since 4 August 2024).
Two MLAs — former AAP Minister Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra — resigned from AAP's primary membership ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election.

BJP president Nitin Nabin accused the Congress of 'protecting three crore infiltrators' during a 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Rohtak on Haryana Foundation Day, countering the INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally over the SIR.

West Bengal's government notified Group D government jobs for one family member of each person killed in political violence over the preceding 25 years (income cutoff ₹50,000/month), a day after CM Suvendu Adhikari's announcement in Paschim Medinipur.

CJI Surya Kant flagged litigants' 'growing tendency' to rush to the Supreme Court for early hearings even as 65,54,788 cases remain pending in High Courts (25 High Courts face 292 judicial vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 1,122) and the Supreme Court's own backlog nears one lakh (97,201 cases).

Sourabh Chandrakar, promoter of the Mahadev Online Book illegal betting app (scam pegged at ₹6,000 crore, run via franchised 'panels' and 'branches'), was extradited to India from Oman following an Interpol Red Corner Notice, in a CBI-led operation.

Foreign Portfolio Investors withdrew ₹34,843 crore from Indian equities in October (second straight month of heavy outflows), per Central Depository Services data, amid concerns over crude oil prices and global interest rates.
EPFO celebrated its 74th Foundation Day; its corpus has grown to over ₹32 lakh crore, accumulated from more than eight crore members, Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya said.

India's headline CPI inflation, which hit multi-year lows in 2025, edged back up to 5.54% by September 2026 — still within the RBI's 2-6% inflation-targeting band, though a reminder that real returns on bank deposits stay thin.
Comex gold fell 7.26% in October to a one-year low of $3,884.9/ounce, while Comex silver dropped 19.1% to $49.13/ounce, as both precious metals posted negative returns for a second straight month.

Iran warned that any renewed war with the US 'could last longer' than the previous round, after President Trump said he had to 'take care of' more targets; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a future conflict would have 'no geographic limitations'.

Brazil's Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a record third presidential term, beating Jair Bolsonaro-backed Flavio Bolsonaro 51.79% to 48.21% in the runoff after trailing in the first round; Lula has backed the New Development Bank and BRICS local-currency trade, while Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro was reportedly taken to the US for trial in January 2026.

Pakistan warned Afghanistan's Taliban government that 'terrorism is a red line' and that Pakistan's national security 'cannot be held hostage to the Taliban regime's inaction', amid deteriorating bilateral ties.
Indian Navy beat Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) 5-4 in a penalty shootout to win the 97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey title in Chennai.

P.V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen won the women's and men's singles titles at the Hylo Open Super 500 (Saarbrucken, Germany) with straight-games final wins — Sindhu's title adds to her earlier Japan Open win this year, and Lakshya ended a title drought.
New Zealand's Glenn Phillips became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series with 341 runs against India in five matches, surpassing England's Phil Salt's 331 (2023).
New Zealand won the fifth T20I by seven wickets (Tim Seifert 93*), but India won the series 3-2 after taking the first three games — captain Shreyas Iyer's first series win in a SENA country.
Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open — his fourth title of the year and 28th overall.
India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.

Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.

India's 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly 13% below the long-term average (87 cm) — the driest season on record (since 1901) for East and Northeast India — despite IMD's April forecast of 92% of the Long Period Average; of seven Indian monsoons since 1950 that coincided with a moderate/strong El Nino, five (including 2026) saw rainfall at least 10% below average, while 1997 was a rare exception because a favourable Indian Ocean Dipole phase offset El Nino's effect; the monsoon supplies about three-quarters of India's annual rainfall and roughly 40% of farmland remains unirrigated.
Manav Thakkar won his first international singles title at WTT Feeder Chennai, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; Sutirtha Mukherjee was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.

The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that Art. 25(1) is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with Art. 21 (right to a healthy environment).
Art. 48A (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; Art. 51A(g) makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.
Op-ed view: celebration is not an 'automatic licence' to expose others to health risks. Regulate with standards and accountability rather than choose between a blanket ban and a free-for-all.

Right to protest vs preventive detention (Jantar Mantar rally stopped at Minto Road): Art. 19(1)(a) and (b) guarantee speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Art. 19(2) and 19(3).

Six States have a Legislative Council: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Art. 169: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority.
Art. 171: Council strength at most one-third of the Assembly and at least 40. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.
Art. 172: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve 6 years; one-third retire every 2 years. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.
Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most four months.
Delay power comes from Art. 197 (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (Art. 198, 14 days).
The Government of India Act, 1935 created bicameral legislatures in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar, Assam. Members then served 9 years.
Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in 1986 (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in 1985 (NTR) and re-created in 2007.
Second ARC (2007) suggested turning Councils into 'councils of local governments' elected only by local body members, to strengthen local self-government.
Debate: supporters see a check on hasty laws and a voice for graduates and teachers; critics see a costly House for defeated leaders. The article says reform them or abolish them.
Three AAP leaders joined the BJP before Punjab's 2027 election: Kunwar Vijay Pratap (Amritsar North, ex-IPS), Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra (Sanour) and Chetan Singh Jauramajra (Samana).

Bihar: independent MLCs Bansidhar Brajwasi (Tirhut Graduates') and Rahul Raj (Saran Teachers') 'joined' the BJP on 31 Oct, then said they only offered support. Jan Suraaj Party asked Council Chairman Ram Bachan Rai to disqualify them.
Tenth Schedule, para 2(2): an independent member who joins a party after election is disqualified. The Presiding Officer decides.
JD(U) expelled Mokama MLA Anant Singh and his wife Neelam Devi for six years for opposing the party's candidate; the Assembly asked him to reply on revoking his membership.
The INDIA bloc held a rally at Ramlila Maidan, Delhi, against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and sought removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. LoP Rahul Gandhi led it.
Editorial: unexplained SIR malpractices could subvert the popular will, and the ECI's silence hurts trust. It also warns against questioning a past election without proof.
Amit Shah claimed SIR removed about 13 crore names: 4.25 crore registered twice, 3 crore dead, 1 crore duplicates, plus 3 crore he called 'infiltrators'. These are his claims.
The ECI will allow judges to e-sign orders on ECINet for West Bengal's 19 appellate tribunals. Over 38 lakh voter cases are pending out of about 60 lakh 'doubtful' cases.
The PM called the Opposition 'avrodh paksh' (obstructionist) seeking 'foreign help'; Rahul Gandhi challenged him to a debate.
SC (CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi) quashed the Rajasthan SEC's order barring civil-society voter awareness before panchayat polls: election bodies have no monopoly on voter awareness.
Counsel argued prohibitory orders under Section 163 BNSS need a real breach of peace. Section 163 replaces old CrPC Section 144.
Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of complicity in urban local body poll rigging; repolls were ordered in only four booths.
State Election Commissions are constitutional bodies under Art. 243K (panchayats) and Art. 243ZA (municipalities).

About 20 National Conference MLAs sent a 10-point memo to Farooq and Omar Abdullah seeking party reforms, manifesto delivery and a stronger push for Statehood. They met at MLA Qaiser Jamsheed Lone's home on 27 Oct.
J&K Deputy CM: Surinder Choudhary. NC general secretary: Ali Muhammad Sagar.
Mehbooba Mufti (PDP): jailing people under UAPA and the Public Safety Act won't solve Kashmir; she wants talks and trade routes to Kashgar and Khotan.
Mains angle: restoration of Statehood, the elected government vs the Lieutenant Governor in a UT, and preventive laws vs political outreach.
UP: Samajwadi Party's PDA = Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak; Akhilesh Yadav now adds 'Pandit' and 'Agarwal'. SP won 5 of 11 MLC seats, BJP the rest.

NCP: six leaders (Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal, Dhananjay Munde, Hasan Mushrif, Dilip Walse Patil) met Amit Shah over the 'authoritarian' style of party president Sunetra Pawar (Maharashtra Deputy CM) and son Parth.
Ajit Pawar died in a helicopter crash earlier in 2026; Sunetra Pawar now heads the NCP.
Karnataka 'sting video' row: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy vs CM D.K. Shivakumar over a video aimed at ex-CM Siddaramaiah.
Congress (Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, K.C. Venugopal) reviewed preparations for the 2027 elections in Uttarakhand and Manipur.
Punjab BJP president: Kewal Singh Dhillon. Punjab's Assembly election is due in early 2027.
The BMC pulled actor Dia Mirza's eco-friendly Deepavali video after BJP objections; Mumbai Mayor: Ritu Tawde.
A Jantar Mantar protester was held under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS (security for keeping the peace; arrest to prevent offences). An FIR named 22 protesters.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaced the CrPC 1973 from 1 July 2024, along with the BNS (for IPC) and the BSA (for the Evidence Act).
SC closed pleas for a CBI probe into the Ram Temple donation fraud after UP's SIT filed a chargesheet. Petitioners may assist the trial court as 'victims of crime'.
Bombay HC (Goa) ordered ₹20 lakh interim compensation each to families of the 25 killed in the Birch by Romeo Lane nightclub fire, Arpora (6 Dec 2025).
Muzaffarnagar riots (2013): a court acquitted eight people in a murder case for lack of evidence.
Delhi HC stayed JNU's dismissal of professor and Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam after a sexual harassment inquiry.
Bombay HC extended its stay on the 'Leave India Notice' to actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an OCI card.
SC told Mokama MLA Anant Singh to surrender by 1 Dec in the Dular Chand Yadav murder case.
Delhi HC (Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre) refused to stay the entry ban on non-BS-VI outside vehicles; next hearing 27 Nov.
VB-G RAM G = Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). It replaced MGNREGA in 2026 under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025.
New grievance rules (Rural Development Ministry): complaints on any matter, logged online the same or next day, inquiry within 7 days, resolution within 15 days or escalation.
Dropped from the May draft: an FIR when there's prima facie financial irregularity, and action-taken reports to local bodies. Critics say this weakens deterrence and local oversight.
MGNREGA's accountability rested on social audit by the Gram Sabha (Section 17 of the old Act).
Census Phase 2 (Population Enumeration) starts 1 Dec 2026 in UP, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab; the rest of India in Jan 2027.
40 questions, 13 new compared with 2011. It is the first digital census, filled on a mobile app by about 34 lakh enumerators.
Registrar General and Census Commissioner: Mritunjay Kumar Narayan. Enumerator training framework: PRAMAN.
The first caste enumeration in independent India (Q.10C): SC/ST pick from a list, others type their caste; there is no separate OBC column. Aadhaar (Q.37) is optional.
Debate: caste data for welfare and reservation, and privacy worries after a trainer linked Aadhaar to citizenship (officials denied it).
Census is a Union List subject (Entry 69); the governing law is the Census Act, 1948.
The Home Ministry plans FRROs in every State capital by 2027. There are now 20, including new ones at Jaipur, Chandigarh, Guwahati, Aizawl and Amravati.
The law behind them: the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, which merged four older laws.
Kerala transferred 35 IAS officers; K.R. Jyothilal became Additional Chief Secretary, Home and Vigilance.
FM Nirmala Sitharaman: public capex will continue until private investment picks up, but 'fiscal prudence is non-negotiable' to protect credit ratings.
Mains angle: the capex multiplier (public spending crowds in private investment) vs the need for fiscal consolidation.
Tamil Nadu set up a committee on welfare and public spending. Op-ed author Anoop Singh was a Member of the 15th Finance Commission.
T.N.'s committed spending was about two-thirds of revenue receipts (2024-25), interest about one-quarter (2025-26), and capex under 1.5% of GSDP.
He suggests State accounts follow the IMF's GFSM 2014. Counting contract staff and aided bodies lifts salary spending from 2.5% to about 4.1% of GDP; hidden subsidies need disclosure.
RBI KYC update camps run 21 Oct to 31 Dec 2026; a self-declaration is enough if nothing has changed.
Congress asked the government to halt the IDBI Bank sale to Fairfax Financial Holdings (Canada) and sought a JPC probe into its valuation.
Sensex closed at 75,682.78 (+1,233) and Nifty 50 at 23,440 (+387.70), both up 1.7%. Reliance jumped 11.6% after Q2 FY27 results.
HSBC India Manufacturing PMI: 54.7 in Oct (55.1 in Sept); export orders at a six-month high. A reading above 50 means expansion.
Tata Sons gave N. Chandrasekaran a third term as chairman (17 Sept). Darius Khambata objected in a letter to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata.
Corporate governance issues at Tata Sons: trustees vs nominee directors, whether to list the company, and liquidity for the Shapoorji Pallonji group.
Petronet LNG Q2 profit rose 53.2% to ₹1,235 crore; dividend ₹7 per share.
US firm Vultr opened a 20-MW AI supercluster in Chennai with about 10,000 AMD MI355X GPUs.
IndiGo (CEO William Walsh) reported a Q2 FY27 loss of about ₹1,879 crore; fares covered only ~60% of the fuel cost rise.
SC (Justices J.B. Pardiwala and Manmohan) upheld enforcement of about $99 million in foreign arbitral awards to Vedanta over the Ravva oilfield (Krishna-Godavari basin).
The dispute came from a 1994 production-sharing contract; the arbitration was seated in Kuala Lumpur under UNCITRAL rules.
SC: governments resisting enforcement undermine India's aim to become an international arbitration hub.
New airfare rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 (notified 31 Oct) let the Centre direct airlines on fares in 'extraordinary situations'. There are no fare caps.
Airlines must file tariffs with the DGCA and show a full fare breakup. Fares have been market-driven since the Air Corporations Act was repealed in 1994.
Mains angle: market pricing vs consumer protection; 'extraordinary situations' is not defined. The rules followed a PIL by S. Laxminarayan.
The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934.
PM Modi opened the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026; India's renewable sector offers about $220 billion in investment opportunities by 2030.
PM: clean energy cushioned India from the West Asia crisis. Next push: storage, indigenous solar hardware, solar in farming, and solar on government buildings.
Russia's LNG exports rose 13.4% to 28 million tonnes (Jan-Oct 2026), helped by the Arctic LNG 2 project.
Natural rubber hit a record ₹300 per kg (RSS-4 grade, Rubber Board price).
Maharashtra approved ₹291.91 crore aid for flood-hit farmers.
CAQM invoked GRAP Stage 2 as Delhi's AQI hit 324 ('very poor'): higher parking fees, staggered office hours, extra Metro trips.
GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) has four stages of emergency measures and is run by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).
Outside vehicles below BS-VI are barred from Delhi until 31 Jan; on day two, 1,228 of 8,263 checked vehicles were turned back.
GRAP is reactive. Lasting fixes need year-round controls on vehicles, dust, industry and crop-residue burning across the airshed.
SC allowed certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR only on 7 and 8 Nov, 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. Bench: Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale.
No crackers within 300 m of hospitals, old age homes, schools and silence zones ('no-cracker zones').
Only CSIR-NEERI / PESO certified makers may produce (2-6 Nov); boxes need QR codes; no series crackers ('ladis') or garlands; sales allowed 4-6 Nov.
North Delhi police seized over 1,200 kg of crackers and filed 10 cases under the Explosives Act; banned crackers were sold under the counter in Sadar Bazar.
SC said the State had 'utterly failed' to enforce its fireworks orders since 2015, and even the complete ban had not improved air quality.
Abroad: Singapore bans private crackers; the UK and Ireland restrict sales to the public; Germany and Sweden require permits.
Stockholm Declaration (1972) linked human well-being to the environment; the Rio Declaration (1992) set the precautionary and polluter-pays principles.
Indian courts and the NGT apply both principles, as in regulating firecrackers.
Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (Arunachal Pradesh), planned at 11.2 GW, is India's answer to China's 60 GW dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India.
A 36-hour bandh shut Upper Siang district against the project; the local Adi community fears losing land. Protests also target the Subansiri Upper project.
Editorial: national need doesn't excuse bypassing laws and local consent. Most of the Brahmaputra's flow comes from monsoon rain and downstream tributaries, not Tibet.
Kuno National Park (MP): a task force found cheetah cub KNG22 was shot by recreational hunters, not wildlife traders.
Indonesia's wildfires burned 1.9 million hectares (Jan-Sep 2026), mostly peatland, worsened by El Nino and the Indian Ocean Dipole.
CREA estimated pollution deaths rose to 5,310 in September. Singapore invoked its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
Cyclone Murasu made landfall between Ongole and Nellore (Andhra Pradesh) with gusts up to 120 km/h; NDRF deployed 14 teams.
Cyclone Arnab forced the evacuation of 1.6 lakh people in Odisha.
Tamil Nadu sent 500 electricity staff in 25 teams to restore power in Andhra Pradesh.
Disaster response chain: IMD warnings, State evacuation, NDRF (a statutory force under the Disaster Management Act, 2005).
Meghalaya got only 38.3 mm of rain in October against a normal of 255 mm, an 85% deficit; the monsoon deficit was 60%.
Ravva oilfield: offshore in the Krishna-Godavari basin, Andhra Pradesh (Vedanta arbitration).
Jhunjhunu (Rajasthan): eight labourers electrocuted when a machine touched an 11-kV line.
Apure (Venezuela), Dammam (Saudi Arabia), Kherson and Oleshky (Ukraine): sites of attacks in the world news.
Iran says it can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets its terms. Hormuz has been blockaded since the war began in February 2026.
Iran's Foreign Minister: Abbas Araghchi; spokesman: Esmaeil Baqaei.
Yemen's Houthis claimed a drone attack on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport.
India link: Hormuz carries much of India's oil and LNG; the war hit Qatar LNG supplies and airline fuel costs.
Justice S. Muralidhar, chair of the UN Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, cited evidence of genocidal acts in Gaza and the largest West Bank displacement since 1967.
He urged universal jurisdiction and limits on arms supplies, and noted that India supplies small arms to Israel.
Knesset: 120 seats, 61 for a majority, 3.25% threshold, proportional representation. Likud won 27 (lowest in 13 years), Yashar 21; turnout 77.7%.
The President gives a leader 28 days (plus 14) to form a government. Hamas's 7 Oct 2023 attack killed about 1,200 people.
US midterm elections on 3 Nov 2026: tariffs and the Iran war (fuel prices) are key issues.
Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932; the race is Roger Marshall vs Adam Hamilton.
Russia resumed strikes on Kherson after a local ceasefire in Oleshky, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, ended.
NSA Ajit Doval held talks in Hanoi with Vietnam's Defence Minister Gen. Phan Van Giang. Relationship status: Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
China's 60 GW Yarlung Tsangpo dam raises fears of flow diversion or sudden release. India and China have no water treaty; China shares flood data only in emergencies.
UK: foreign care workers who arrived before May 2025 can get indefinite leave to remain after 5 years (not 15) if they earn £25,000+. Home Secretary: Shabana Mahmood.
Five Visakhapatnam youths were allegedly tricked into joining the Russian army.
The UN General Assembly again adopted a resolution against the US embargo on Cuba; India voted as before and did not abstain.
Venezuela's army attacked a camp of Colombia's ELN (National Liberation Army) in Apure state; at least 19 killed.
Contracts worth ₹53,866.50 crore for 8 Next Generation Corvettes: GRSE builds 5, Goa Shipyard 3. First Navy-designed warships built by Defence PSUs.
Atmanirbhar defence: about 72 lakh person-days of direct jobs; the corvettes handle anti-submarine, anti-surface and coastal roles.
Over 100 Delhi Police personnel protested the transfers of ACP Manasvi Vashistha and SHO Arun Kumar after a lawyer-police scuffle on 23 Oct. Commissioner: Anurag Kumar.
Police demanded an SOP for confrontations with lawyers, raising issues of police reform and accountability on both sides.
MP police Inspector Dilip Puri was run over by a truck smuggling illicit liquor (Dewas).
Coast Guard ship ICGS C-448 rescued a fisherman 100 km off Mangaluru.
The ED searched 14 premises of ex-Punjab minister Sunder Sham Arora under the PMLA.
Former T.N. School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi is in CCB custody over alleged bribes of ₹400 crore for school recognition.
Hackers raised supermarket freezer temperatures to 50°C in Sweden and other European countries.
DPDP Act 2023; Rules notified Nov 2025; fully in force May 2027. Earlier: IT Act 2000 and 2011 Rules. Privacy was declared a fundamental right in 2017.
Gaps in the DPDP Act: no 'sensitive data' category, no cover for public data, silence on AI training, a weak right to be forgotten, and a broad research exemption.
Suggested fixes: a right to object, a sensitive-data category, and erasure duties. The author warns against banning AI training outright.
UCLA's optical-electronic deepfake detector (journal eLight): 99.86% accurate on fakes, 95.72% on real videos, 94.8% on Google Veo 3 clips; the optical part uses 7x less energy.
People spot deepfakes only about 50% of the time (Nature Communications).
Kavli Prize to Vasily Belokurov, Amina Helmi and Rodrigo Ibata for discovering the Milky Way's past galaxy mergers.
Milky Way mergers: Sagittarius dwarf (~6 bn years ago), Gaia-Enceladus (~10 bn, found with ESA's Gaia), Kraken-Heracles (~12 bn). The Magellanic Clouds are being absorbed now.
Sputnik 2 (launched 3 Nov 1957) carried Laika, the first animal to orbit Earth.
Mariner 10 (launched 3 Nov 1973) was the first probe to Mercury.
Study (PNAS): cigarette smoke causes epigenetic changes in lung organoids and silences the Zbp1 gene. Then a Kras mutation leads to adenocarcinoma and Tp53 loss to squamous cell carcinoma.
Many Indian lung-cancer patients are non-smokers exposed to air pollution and biomass smoke, so tobacco control must go with clean air and clean cooking.
3 Nov in science: Alzheimer presented his patient (1906); the SOS signal was adopted in Berlin (1906); the first UNIX manual came out (1971).

SC (Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh): aid to freed bonded labourers within 7 days; verify complaints in 24 hours; release certificate in 24 hours; States to adopt the SOP within 6 months.
The Court called identification, release and rehabilitation a 'continuing constitutional obligation'.
Law: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976. Art. 23 bans forced labour.
POCSO: Kasaragod paediatrician Dr P. Krishnan (78) was sentenced to 47 years, running concurrently as 20 years, for sexually assaulting a 15-year-old patient.
India Hate Lab recorded 60 attacks on Christians in West Bengal (13 May to 20 Sept); a People's Tribunal heard survivors.
Fire at the HPCL Visakh Refinery (Residue Upgradation Facility), Visakhapatnam; no casualties.
India, in the news: CJI Surya Kant; Solicitor-General Tushar Mehta; CEC Gyanesh Kumar; RGI Mritunjay Kumar Narayan; NSA Ajit Doval; FM Nirmala Sitharaman; Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar.
World, in the news: Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu; Iran FM Abbas Araghchi; UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood; Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto; Vietnam Defence Minister Phan Van Giang.
National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, since 2014) is on 31 Oct, Sardar Patel's birth anniversary. Statue of Unity: 182 m, inaugurated 2018.
Kavli Prize (astrophysics): Vasily Belokurov, Amina Helmi, Rodrigo Ibata, for discovering past mergers of the Milky Way.
Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes, Italy) became the youngest F1 champion at 20 years 68 days, finishing 3rd in the Mexico City GP won by Max Verstappen.
Previous youngest champion: Sebastian Vettel (23 years 134 days, 2010). Antonelli is the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari (1953).
Glenn Maxwell retired from international cricket: 7 Tests, 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is.
Tilak Varma will captain India A in the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup.
IPL: retention deadline 17 Nov; mini auction in Goa on 16 Dec.
Ranji Trophy: Services captain Rajat Paliwal scored 111* vs Delhi at Palam. Jammu & Kashmir won last season's title under Paras Dogra.
Asian Champions Trophy: India beat Korea 8-0 in Jalandhar; the knockouts move to Mohali.
The WTA 250 Chennai Open's first day was washed out by Cyclone Murasu.
Archery Premier League: 15-second shot clock (20 s at World Cups). USA's Casey Kaufhold (Paris 2024 medallist) plays for Chero Archers with Kumkum Mohod (Asian Games champion) and Atanu Das.
The 10th leg of Season 2 of the Indian Golf Premier League is in Visakhapatnam.
